## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- Two occurrences of the same token can start with the same embedding. Their ranks in the sequence provide information distinct from token identity.
- An additive absolute encoding can combine the token embedding with a vector for its position at the input.
- RoPE uses position to rotate Q and K after projection. Their dot product then depends on the relative offset.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

After tokenization, swap the positions of two IDs in the sequence. Do their rows in the embedding table change?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No, their IDs select the same rows. Their sequence positions change, which can affect the resulting contextual states.

</details>
